card.title: How much can you hold in mind?

body.question: About how many separate chunks of information can the average adult hold in working memory at once?
body.reveal: Research since the 2000s suggests about four chunks, not the 'seven plus or minus two' from the famous 1956 paper. Chunking, like grouping digits in a phone number, is how we stretch it.

claims.quote: Cowan proposed that working memory has a capacity of about four chunks in young adults
